**A 36-hour ship-loader outage on 17 August drove USD 30,519 in demurrage, and the data shows that timing matters critically: the same 36-hour outage hitting the quarter's last vessel (VC-0127) would have deferred 177,700 tonnes and USD 19.1 million in revenue, slashing Q1 FY2027 EBITDA by USD 17.7 million—yet incurred no extra demurrage because the vessel simply slips into the next quarter.**

| Scenario | Outage (h) | Deferred tonnes | Deferred revenue (USD) | Demurrage from outage (USD) | Quarter EBITDA (USD) | EBITDA change (USD) | Source |
|----------|------------|-----------------|------------------------|----------------------------|----------------------|---------------------|--------|
| Real (VC-0115, mid-quarter) | 36 | 0 | 0 | 30,519 | 373.1M | 0 | OPS · SAP_STANDIN · SAP |
| What-if (VC-0127, quarter-end) | 36 | 177,700 | 19,143,621 | 25,107 | 355.4M | –17.7M | OPS · SAP_STANDIN · SAP |

**The golden thread** links the failure—SL-01 loader down (SAP notification 000010005910, 18 Aug 2026, SAP)—to a **spare stockout** (motor MZ-SP-A101, 0 units, sole supplier 0017300001, SAP_STANDIN), 36 hours of vessel delay (OPS), and the quarter's USD 274,750 total demurrage (MIXED: operations, SAP_STANDIN, SAP). Port stock remained healthy (~2.59 Mt average in Aug, OPS), so buffer wasn't the issue; **spare availability and outage timing** were.

**Next step:** Secure safety stock for motor MZ-SP-A101 from supplier 0017300001 and establish a quarter-end vessel priority protocol to defer non-critical ships early if an outage looms, protecting revenue recognition.
